questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best games for children to play at school
'Junk' playgrounds and why free play matters
How to make playgrounds completely safe
The history of football in British streets
questions.why: They discuss adventure playgrounds and how they give kids the freedom and space to play.

questions.q: What were Pippa's and Phil's favourite childhood games?
options: They both loved football
Phil liked skipping and Pippa liked football
Pippa liked skipping, and Phil preferred football
They both liked hide and seek
questions.why: Pippa loved skipping; Phil couldn't skip, so he preferred football.

questions.q: Where did many children in British cities play 80 years ago?
options: In the ruins of houses destroyed in the war
In large city parks with swings and slides
On the beach during the summer holidays
In school gyms after lessons had finished
questions.why: Phil says it was common for children to play in bombsites, ruins from World War II.

questions.q: How are adventure playgrounds different from normal playgrounds?
options: They have more swings and slides than usual
They are only for older children and teens
They are indoors, so they are open all year
Children use materials to build things
questions.why: Unlike fixed swings and slides, they provide building materials for kids to build things.

questions.q: What does reporter William Kremer see when he looks more closely at the playground?
options: Nothing but rubbish and broken furniture
Children building things and playing freely
Adults fixing the broken equipment
Children sitting quietly and reading
questions.why: Looking closer, he sees homemade structures and hidey-holes, and children swinging on ropes.

questions.q: According to Dr Anna Housley Juster, how important is play?
options: It matters much less than school work
It's only important for very young children
After basic needs, it's the most important
It's more important than food and shelter
questions.why: She says after basic needs, 'play is by far the most important factor for healthy child development'.

questions.q: Which skills does Anna say children develop through free play?
options: Confidence, resilience and ways of coping
Reading and writing skills for school
Maths and science skills for later life
Building real houses as adults
questions.why: She says kids build resiliency, confidence, coping strategies and regulation strategies in play.

questions.q: Why does Pippa mention the small dangers in adventure playgrounds, like nails and sharp metal?
options: To warn parents to keep their children away
To say the playgrounds should be closed
To show that the playgrounds are badly built
To explain that small risks build resilience
questions.why: She says taking small risks with these makes kids more resilient and builds coping strategies.
